body.title: fix(df): keep the system CAs in the proxy CA bundle
body.description:
## Description

Most of the variables glab points at its CA bundle replace a tool's default trust instead of extending it: `PIP_CERT`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `TWINE_CERT`, `BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT` and `CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO`. !4505 adds npm's `cafile`. When the user has no CA of their own, the bundle holds only glab's CA.

glab intercepts every connection that goes through its proxy, so those need only glab's CA. But a connection that skips the proxy and reads one of these variables can no longer verify any public host. Since !4503, a script run with `glab dependency-firewall poetry run` that connects with `PIP_CERT` fails this way. Once !4505 points npm's `cafile` at the bundle, so does an install script that downloads with npm's settings, because Node's `https` and `fetch` ignore proxy variables by default.

The bundle now also holds the system roots:

| Code | Change |
|---|---|
| `writeCABundle` in `pm.go` | Appends the system roots after the user's CAs and glab's CA |
| `Run` in `pm.go` | Passes `systemRoots()`, which the JVM truststore already uses. It reads PEM bundle files on Linux, the keychains on macOS and the certificate stores on Windows |
| `systemRoots` in `jvmtrust.go` | Reads the roots once per process, so Windows starts PowerShell at most once, and logs when it finds none. On macOS it keeps only CA certificates, so the device and MDM certificates in the System keychain don't become trust anchors |
| `SystemCABundlePaths` in `jvmtrust.go` | One list of Linux CA bundle paths, Go's six locations. The CI job proxy's merged bundle (`session.WriteMergedBundle`), which already includes the system roots for the same reason, now reads the same list |
| `encodeJVMTrustStore` in `jvmtrust.go` | Skips system roots the bundle already holds, so Maven and Gradle don't get each root twice |
| Help text and docs | Say that the CA bundle also holds the system's trusted certificates |

On macOS, reading the roots takes about 0.03 s and adds 163 certificates to the temporary bundle, which comes to 246 KB. If no roots can be read, the bundle is the same as before. Windows reads them with PowerShell, which hasn't been timed.

A user who narrowed a tool's trust to their own CA, for example with `PIP_CERT`, now also trusts the system CAs for connections that skip glab's proxy. The JVM truststore already works this way.

This MR should land before !4505, which would otherwise break those install scripts for every npm user without a `cafile`.

## Related Issues

Related to gitlab-org&24327

## How has this been tested?

<details><summary>Unit tests and direct connections before and after</summary>

Unit tests in `internal/dependencyfirewall/pm`:

- `TestWriteCABundleAppendsSystemRoots`: the bundle holds glab's CA, then the roots passed in.
- `TestEncodeJVMTrustStoreListsEachRootOnce`: a system root that is already in the bundle isn't added to the JVM truststore again.
- `TestSystemRootsHoldOnlyCAsOnMacOS`: on macOS, every system root is a CA certificate.
- The existing `writeCABundle` tests pass no roots and keep their exact counts. `TestRunMergesUserCAIntoOverriddenVar` goes through `Run`, so its count now includes the system roots.

`go test` over `internal/dependencyfirewall/...` and `internal/commands/df/...` and golangci-lint pass.

Direct connections on macOS with no CA settings of the user's own, comparing `main` (`b923f6be9`) with this branch (`c6267c35a`). The probes ran with Python 3.14.6 and Poetry 2.5.1, and with Node 24.19.0 and npm 11.17.0.

| Case | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `glab df poetry run python probe.py`, where `probe.py` connects to pypi.org with Python's `http.client` and `PIP_CERT` as its CA file | `PIP_CERT` holds 1 certificate; `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` | 164 certificates; status `200` |

With !4505 (`0674248f7`), `glab df npm install` in a project whose `postinstall` script connects to registry.npmjs.org with Node's `https` and npm's `cafile`:

| Binary | `npm_config_cafile` | Direct connection |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | Unset | `200` |
| !4505 | 1 certificate | `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY` |
| !4505 with this branch | 164 certificates | `200` |

The install itself succeeds in all three cases, because npm's own requests go through glab's proxy.

`probe.py`:

```python
import http.client, os, ssl
f = os.environ["PIP_CERT"]
print("PROBE PIP_CERT has", open(f).read().count("BEGIN CERTIFICATE"), "certificate(s)")
try:
    c = http.client.HTTPSConnection("pypi.org", context=ssl.create_default_context(cafile=f), timeout=10)
    c.request("HEAD", "/simple/six/")
    print("PROBE direct connection status", c.getresponse().status)
except Exception as e:
    print("PROBE direct connection error", type(e).__name__, str(e)[:90])
```

The npm `postinstall` script, `probe.js`:

```javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const https = require('https');
const f = process.env.npm_config_cafile;
let ca;
if (f) {
  ca = fs.readFileSync(f);
  console.log('PROBE npm_config_cafile has ' + (ca.toString().match(/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/g) || []).length + ' certificate(s)');
} else {
  console.log('PROBE npm_config_cafile unset');
}
https.get({ host: 'registry.npmjs.org', path: '/left-pad', ca, agent: false }, (r) => {
  console.log('PROBE direct connection status ' + r.statusCode);
  r.resume();
}).on('error', (e) => console.log('PROBE direct connection error ' + (e.code || e.message)));
```

</details>

body.title: feat(minder): upload only agent activity from after setup
body.description:
## Description

By default, glab minder now uploads only agent activity from after the user set up each agent with `glab minder setup`. Before this change, resuming a Claude Code, OpenCode or Cursor conversation from before setup uploaded its earlier turns, and the fallback sync uploaded Codex and Cursor sessions from the last 89 days.

Setup records when it first set up each agent in a new file next to the existing agent lists, once the user confirms. Running setup again keeps the first time. The new `--include-history` flag also uploads the last 89 days for the agents a setup sets up for the first time. An agent set up earlier keeps what it uploads, because a later setup cannot bring back what was skipped. Setup refuses the flag when every agent is set up already, and says how to start again. The setup prompt says exactly which activity is uploaded for each agent: from now on, from when it was first set up, or from the last 89 days.

For Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex, sync leaves out transcript entries timestamped before setup, in both the hooks and the fallback sync. For a session that started before setup it also leaves out the goal taken from an earlier prompt and the start time. A tool call made before setup is left out together with its result, even when the result arrives after setup. A session whose syncing starts partway through its transcript takes its goal from its first prompt after setup. Claude Code compaction summaries are no longer uploaded as prompts, because they can describe the conversation from before setup. A transcript that was last active before setup is skipped to its end the first time glab sees it, so later turns of a resumed session are still uploaded without reading old transcripts on every run.

Cursor transcripts have no timestamps. When setup first sets up Cursor, it records where each existing Cursor transcript ends, as the point its syncing starts. A resumed conversation from before setup then uploads exactly the turns added after setup, and a transcript created after setup uploads from its beginning. Setup fails and records nothing for Cursor if it cannot read a workspace or transcript, so no transcript is left out. With `--include-history`, setup records this only for transcripts unchanged for longer than 89 days. A chat that Cursor copies under a new ID counts as new. The help text says so. Setup and sync share the code that lists Cursor transcripts and the code that keeps each session's sync position.

A hook sync that cannot read a session's sync position now fails instead of uploading the transcript from its beginning. A session that glab has uploaded nothing for is no longer created on GitLab only to be marked completed. The agent files are now replaced atomically.

Agents set up by an earlier glab version have no recorded time. They keep the 89-day behaviour until the user runs setup again, and the help text says so. `glab minder setup --uninstall` removes the setup times and the Cursor snapshot along with the rest of the local state.

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8776

## How has this been tested?

New unit tests cover:

- Claude Code through the hook and through the fallback sync, including a compaction summary.
- A Codex session that runs across setup, and a Codex session from before setup that is resumed.
- An OpenCode session from before setup.
- Cursor transcripts from before and after setup, through the fallback sync and through the hook.
- A sync position that cannot be read.
- A tool call that spans setup, with its result in the same sync or a later one, and the goal of a resumed Claude Code, Codex and Cursor session.
- Completing a session with and without earlier uploads.
- The setup snapshot: taken on first setup and not on re-runs, limited to old transcripts with `--include-history`, following symlinked workspaces, and failing on an unreadable workspace.
- `--include-history` on a re-run, agents set up by an earlier glab version, an unreadable setup file, the setup prompt for each case, and uninstall removing the new state.

`go test ./internal/commands/govern/...` passes, and so does `go test -race` on the sync, setup and shared packages. `golangci-lint run ./internal/commands/govern/...` passes for macOS, Linux and Windows.

body.title: feat(stack): support merge request description templates
body.description:
## Description

Add `glab stack sync --template <name>` for teams that use a standard merge request description. The flag uses the same local template loader as `glab mr create`, appends each diff's commit body after the template, and applies to newly created merge requests. Template errors are detected before fetching or pushing. The flag is optional and sync retains its current description behavior when the flag is omitted.

Closes #8751.

## Testing

- Ran the stack command suites, shared command utilities, and merge request creation tests.
- Checked that two new merge requests get the same template, preserve their own commit message bodies, and handle an empty body. The missing-template test exercises the CLI flag and verifies sync exits before creation.
- Built the CLI, verified its help, regenerated reference documentation, and ran lint.

This contribution contains AI-assisted code and was validated with local tests.

body.title: fix(df): keep npm and Yarn cafile settings from distrusting the proxy
body.description:
## Description

When a user points npm, pnpm or Yarn at their company CA with a `cafile`, that setting replaces the CA bundle glab gives the package manager. It then rejects glab's inspection proxy, and the install fails. It fails closed, so nothing gets past the firewall, but nothing installs either.

### Example

A developer behind a company's TLS-inspecting proxy has `npm_config_cafile=/etc/corp/ca.pem` set, so npm trusts the company CA. They run `glab dependency-firewall npm install left-pad`.

On `main`:

1. glab starts its inspection proxy and writes its CA bundle: glab's CA and the system CAs.
1. glab gives npm `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<bundle>` and points its proxy settings at glab.
1. npm reads `npm_config_cafile` and passes `/etc/corp/ca.pem` to Node as the complete CA list. Node then ignores `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, so glab's CA is gone.
1. npm rejects glab's proxy certificate with `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`, and nothing installs.
1. Even if npm trusted glab, glab's own connection to the registry, through the company proxy, wouldn't trust `/etc/corp/ca.pem`. glab doesn't read `npm_config_cafile`.

With this MR:

1. glab merges `/etc/corp/ca.pem` into its bundle, which then holds the company CA, glab's CA and the system CAs.
1. glab sets `npm_config_cafile` and `NPM_CONFIG_CAFILE` to that bundle, empties `NPM_CONFIG_CA`, and removes other spellings of these variables. Environment variables outrank every `.npmrc`, so the bundle wins wherever the user's `cafile` was set.
1. npm trusts glab's proxy, and glab checks the package against the policy.
1. glab's registry connection trusts the file in `npm_config_cafile`, so it gets through the company proxy, and the package installs.
1. Install scripts that read npm's `cafile` get the same bundle, so they trust the company CA and public hosts.

### What glab does

| | `main` | This MR |
|---|---|---|
| What npm, pnpm and Yarn get | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<bundle>` | The same, plus `npm_config_cafile` and `NPM_CONFIG_CAFILE` pointing at the bundle. npm and pnpm also get an empty `NPM_CONFIG_CA`. Yarn 1 gets `YARN_CAFILE=<bundle>`, but only if the user set `YARN_CAFILE`. Other spellings of these variables are removed |
| Yarn Berry plugin | Empties the per-host `networkSettings` | Also points `httpsCaFilePath` (Yarn 4) or `caFilePath` (Yarn 3) at the bundle, if the user set one. Berry rejects these variables on versions that lack them, so they can't go in the environment |
| What the bundle holds | The user's `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` file, glab's CA and the system CAs | Also the files in `npm_config_cafile`, `NPM_CONFIG_CAFILE`, `YARN_CAFILE`, `YARN_HTTPS_CA_FILE_PATH` and `YARN_CA_FILE_PATH`, in any spelling |
| What glab's own registry connections trust | System CAs, the `ca_cert` setting, and `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `PIP_CERT`, `TWINE_CERT`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT` and `CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO`, exact names only | Also the five npm and Yarn variables above, in any spelling |

glab reads these variables in any case, as npm and Yarn do, so it scans the environment itself rather than using `os.LookupEnv`, which only matches exact names. The help text lists them, and `docs/source/` is regenerated.

These still fail closed:

- pnpm 11 and later, which this MR doesn't cover.
- A `cafile` in Yarn 1's `.yarnrc` without `YARN_CAFILE`. Overriding it needs `YARN_CAFILE`, which Berry rejects.
- A per-registry `//host/:ca` in pnpm's `.npmrc`.
- A CA named only in `.npmrc` or `.yarnrc(.yml)`, for registry connections. Set glab's `ca_cert` to it.

### Trade-off

A user who set `cafile` to limit npm to their company CA now has npm trust the company CA, glab's CA and the system CAs. npm's own requests all go to glab's proxy, so in practice this matters only for install scripts that connect directly. The CA bundle for every package manager has worked this way since !4514.

Split from !4281 (closed), with the Poetry fix in !4503 and the Bundler fix in !4504, both now merged.

## Related Issues

Related to gitlab-org&24327

## How has this been tested?

<details><summary>Unit tests and before/after runs behind a corporate proxy</summary>

Unit tests in `internal/dependencyfirewall/pm`:

- `TestManagerExistingBundleVars`, `TestManagerEnvironAndCATrust`, `TestNPMCATrust` and `TestRunPassesRunInputsToSetup`.
- `TestRunMergesUserCAIntoOverriddenVar` (npm, pnpm and Yarn) and `TestRunTrustsNPMAndYarnCAVarsInAnyCase`.
- `TestRunPointsNPMCafileAtBundle`, `TestRunDropsInheritedNPMInlineCA`, `TestRunReplacesInheritedYarnCafileInAnyCase`, `TestRunMergesYarnBerryCAFileIntoBundle` and `TestYarnSetupSetsYarnCafileOnlyWhenInherited`.
- `TestWriteCABundleSkipsEmptyVariable`, `TestWriteCABundleMergesEverySpelling`, `TestUpstreamRootCAsMatchesNPMAndYarnNamesInAnyCase` and `TestUpstreamRootCAsMatchesOtherNamesExactly`.

`go test` over `internal/dependencyfirewall/...` and `internal/commands/df/...` and golangci-lint pass.

Before and after, run on this branch (`46194a283`) against `main` at its base (`7ea9c2ebc`), on macOS with npm 11.17.0 (Node.js 24.19.0), pnpm 10.34.9, Yarn 1.22.22 and Yarn 4.18.1. The package managers ran behind a TLS-intercepting corporate proxy (mitmproxy in Docker), with its CA set as the company CA in the package manager's own setting. glab trusted that proxy through `GLAB_CA_CERT`, except in the `npm_config_cafile` case. "Corporate proxy" counts the requests that proxy logged during the run with this branch.

| Case | `main` | This branch | Corporate proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| npm, `cafile` in `.npmrc` | `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`, exit 1 | `added 1 package` | 2 |
| npm, `npm_config_cafile` only, no `GLAB_CA_CERT` | `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`, exit 1 | `added 1 package` | 2 |
| pnpm 10.34.9, `cafile` in `.npmrc` | Hangs with no output | `Done in 1.4s using pnpm v10.34.9` | 2 |
| Yarn 1.22.22, `YARN_CAFILE` | `error Error: self-signed certificate in certificate chain`, exit 1 | `success Saved 1 new dependency.` | 2 to 4 |
| Yarn 4.18.1, `httpsCaFilePath` in `.yarnrc.yml` | `YN0001: RequestError: self-signed certificate in certificate chain`, exit 1 | `YN0000: · Done` | 2 |
| No CA settings; a `postinstall` script connects to registry.npmjs.org directly with npm's `cafile` | `npm_config_cafile` unset; status `200` | 164 certificates, glab's CA and the system's; status `200` | n/a |

Without glab, npm with the `.npmrc` `cafile` installs through the corporate proxy, so the setup itself works.

On !4281's last head (`bdff30ccc`), the same changes also passed these on Linux in Docker, with npm 10.9.9: `NPM_CONFIG_CAFILE`, `npm_config_cafile` plus an inline `npm_config_ca`, Yarn 1 with a `.npmrc` `cafile`, and Yarn 4 with `YARN_HTTPS_CA_FILE_PATH`.

From the same runs on !4281, these still fail closed:

- pnpm 11.28.12 with a `.npmrc` `cafile`, and a `cafile` in Yarn 1's `.yarnrc`, both fail with a TLS error.
- With the company CA only in `.npmrc` and no `GLAB_CA_CERT`, glab prints `warning: dependency firewall request to registry registry.npmjs.org:443 failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`.

And these don't reproduce, so they install on `main` too:

- Yarn 3.8.7 doesn't apply `caFilePath` to requests through a proxy.
- pnpm 10.34.9 doesn't apply a per-registry `:cafile` under glab.

</details>


<details><summary>Manual testing steps (bash or zsh)</summary>

These steps compare this branch with `main` at the branch's base. glab, npm, pnpm and Yarn run on your machine, and mitmproxy runs in Docker as a TLS-intercepting corporate proxy on port 8081. pnpm 10.34.9, Yarn 1.22.22 and Yarn 4.18.1 come from corepack, with its files kept in the scratch directory. Run the steps from the root of a checkout of this branch, with Docker and Node.js 20 to 24 (which ship corepack), in a new terminal tab: they set a fake token and proxy settings. Each step is one command, even when it spans several lines.

| Case | Steps | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 39–40 | npm with `cafile` in `.npmrc`, without glab: installs | Same |
| B/C | 41–42 | npm, `cafile` in `.npmrc`: `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN` | Installs |
| D | 43–49 | npm, `npm_config_cafile` only, no `GLAB_CA_CERT`: fails | Installs; glab's registry connection trusts the file too |
| E | 50–52 | pnpm 10, `cafile` in `.npmrc`: hangs | Installs |
| F | 53–57 | Yarn 1, `YARN_CAFILE`: `self-signed certificate in certificate chain` | Installs |
| G | 58–60 | Yarn 4, `httpsCaFilePath`: `YN0001: RequestError` | Installs |
| H | 61–63 | No CA settings; an install script connects directly with npm's `cafile`: `200` | `200`, with the system CAs in the file |

**1. Name a scratch directory**

```shell
T=~/df-4505-test
```

**2. Name this checkout**

```shell
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

**3. Create the scratch directories**

```shell
mkdir -p $T/mitm $T/bin $T/npm $T/npm-env $T/pnpm $T/yarn1 $T/yarn4 $T/probe
```

**4. Build this branch**

```shell
make -C $W build
```

**5. Keep this branch's binary**

```shell
cp $W/bin/glab $T/glab-branch
```

**6. Check out `main` at this branch's base**

```shell
git -C $W worktree add --detach $T/main "$(git -C $W merge-base HEAD origin/main)"
```

**7. Build `main`**

```shell
make -C $T/main build
```

**8. Keep `main`'s binary**

```shell
cp $T/main/bin/glab $T/glab-main
```

**9. Start the corporate proxy**

```shell
docker run -d --name df-4505-corp -p 127.0.0.1:8081:8080 \
  -v $T/mitm:/home/mitmproxy/.mitmproxy mitmproxy/mitmproxy mitmdump
```

**10. Wait for the proxy to create its CA**

```shell
sleep 3
```

**11. Name the corporate CA.** The `ls` on the next step prints its path; if it doesn't, wait a second and run it again.

```shell
CA=$T/mitm/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem
```

**12. Check that the CA exists**

```shell
ls $CA
```

**13. Keep corepack's and Yarn's own files in the scratch directory**

```shell
export COREPACK_HOME=$T/corepack COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0 YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER=$T/yarn-global
```

**14. Create pnpm and Yarn shims in the scratch directory**

```shell
corepack enable --install-directory $T/bin pnpm yarn
```

**15. Put the shims first on `PATH`**

```shell
export PATH=$T/bin:$PATH
```

**16. Create the npm project**

```shell
printf '{"name":"df-npm","version":"1.0.0","private":true}\n' > $T/npm/package.json
```

**17. Point npm at the corporate CA in the project's `.npmrc`**

```shell
printf 'cafile=%s\n' $CA > $T/npm/.npmrc
```

**18. Create a second npm project, without `.npmrc`**

```shell
cp $T/npm/package.json $T/npm-env/package.json
```

**19. Create the pnpm project, pinned to pnpm 10**

```shell
printf '{"name":"df-pnpm","version":"1.0.0","private":true,"packageManager":"pnpm@10.34.9"}\n' > $T/pnpm/package.json
```

**20. Point pnpm at the corporate CA**

```shell
cp $T/npm/.npmrc $T/pnpm/.npmrc
```

**21. Create the Yarn 1 project**

```shell
printf '{"name":"df-yarn1","version":"1.0.0","private":true,"packageManager":"yarn@1.22.22"}\n' > $T/yarn1/package.json
```

**22. Create the Yarn 4 project**

```shell
printf '{"name":"df-yarn4","version":"1.0.0","private":true,"packageManager":"yarn@4.18.1"}\n' > $T/yarn4/package.json
```

**23. Point Yarn 4 at the corporate CA in `.yarnrc.yml`**

```shell
printf 'httpsCaFilePath: %s\n' $CA > $T/yarn4/.yarnrc.yml
```

**24. Create the probe project.** Its `postinstall` script connects to registry.npmjs.org directly, without the proxy, using npm's `cafile`, like an install script that downloads a binary.

```shell
printf '{"name":"df-probe","version":"1.0.0","private":true,"dependencies":{"left-pad":"1.3.0"},"scripts":{"postinstall":"node probe.js"}}\n' > $T/probe/package.json
```

**25. Write the probe script**

```shell
printf '%s\n' 'const f=process.env.npm_config_cafile;const ca=f?require("fs").readFileSync(f):undefined;console.log("PROBE npm_config_cafile "+(f?"has "+(ca.toString().match(/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/g)||[]).length+" certificates":"unset"));require("https").get({host:"registry.npmjs.org",path:"/left-pad",ca,agent:false},r=>{console.log("PROBE direct connection status "+r.statusCode);r.resume()}).on("error",e=>console.log("PROBE direct connection error "+(e.code||e.message)))' > $T/probe/probe.js
```

**26. Go into the pnpm project.** Its `packageManager` field picks pnpm 10.34.9.

```shell
cd $T/pnpm
```

**27. Download pnpm and check its version.** Prints `10.34.9`.

```shell
pnpm --version
```

**28. Go into the Yarn 1 project**

```shell
cd $T/yarn1
```

**29. Download Yarn 1 and check its version.** Prints `1.22.22`.

```shell
yarn --version
```

**30. Go into the Yarn 4 project**

```shell
cd $T/yarn4
```

**31. Download Yarn 4 and check its version.** Prints `4.18.1`.

```shell
yarn --version
```

**32. Clear CA, proxy and package-manager settings from your shell**

```shell
unset NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS SSL_CERT_FILE GLAB_CA_CERT HTTP_PROXY http_proxy https_proxy ALL_PROXY NO_PROXY no_proxy CI GITLAB_CI \
  npm_config_cafile NPM_CONFIG_CAFILE npm_config_ca NPM_CONFIG_CA YARN_CAFILE YARN_HTTPS_CA_FILE_PATH YARN_CA_FILE_PATH
```

**33. Send traffic through the corporate proxy**

```shell
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8081
```

**34. Let glab allow every package without calling GitLab**

```shell
export GLAB_DF_FAKE_DEFAULT=allow GITLAB_REPO=gitlab.com/example/df-proxy-test GITLAB_TOKEN=fake
```

**35. Keep your own glab settings out of the test, and let glab trust the corporate proxy**

```shell
export GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=$T/glab-config GLAB_SEND_TELEMETRY=false GLAB_CHECK_UPDATE=false GLAB_CA_CERT=$CA
```

**36. Keep the package managers' caches in the scratch directory, and make failures quick**

```shell
export npm_config_cache=$T/npm-cache npm_config_store_dir=$T/pnpm-store npm_config_cache_dir=$T/pnpm-cache \
  npm_config_fetch_retries=0 npm_config_audit=false npm_config_fund=false npm_config_update_notifier=false \
  YARN_CACHE_FOLDER=$T/yarn-cache YARN_ENABLE_GLOBAL_CACHE=0 YARN_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=0 COREPACK_ENABLE_NETWORK=0
```

**37. Define `corp`.** It counts the requests the corporate proxy has logged.


**38. Define `try`.** It deletes the project's installed packages, lockfiles and caches, so every install downloads again, then runs the command and prints its exit code and the number of requests the corporate proxy saw.

```shell
try() {

    $T/npm-cache $T/pnpm-store $T/pnpm-cache $T/yarn-cache $T/yarn-global

}
```

```shell
cd $T/npm
```

**42. C: install through this branch.** Expect `added 1 package` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +2 requests`.

**43. D: go into the project without `.npmrc`**

**45. D: point npm at the corporate CA with `npm_config_cafile` only**


**46. D: install through `main`.** Expect `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN` and `exit=1, corporate proxy: +0 requests`.

```shell

```

**47. D: install through this branch.** Expect `added 1 package` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +2 requests`. glab's own registry connection now trusts the file in `npm_config_cafile`.

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df npm install left-pad
```

**48. D: drop `npm_config_cafile`**

```shell

```

**49. D: let glab trust the corporate proxy again**

```shell
export GLAB_CA_CERT=$CA
```

**50. E: go into the pnpm project**

```shell
cd $T/pnpm
```

**51. E: install through `main`.** pnpm hangs without printing anything. After about 30 seconds, stop it with Control+C.


**52. E: install through this branch.** Expect `Done in …s using pnpm v10.34.9` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +2 requests`.


**53. F: go into the Yarn 1 project**

```shell

```

**54. F: point Yarn 1 at the corporate CA with `YARN_CAFILE`**

```shell

```

**55. F: install through `main`.** Expect `error Error: self-signed certificate in certificate chain` and `exit=1, corporate proxy: +0 requests`.

```shell
try $T/glab-main df yarn add left-pad
```

**56. F: install through this branch.** Expect `success Saved 1 new dependency.` and `exit=0`, with 2 or more requests through the corporate proxy.

```shell

```

**57. F: drop `YARN_CAFILE`**


**58. G: go into the Yarn 4 project**

**59. G: install through `main`.** Expect `YN0001: RequestError: self-signed certificate in certificate chain` and `exit=1, corporate proxy: +0 requests`.

**60. G: install through this branch.** Expect `YN0000: · Done` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +2 requests`.

**61. H: go into the probe project**



**63. H: install through this branch.** Expect `PROBE npm_config_cafile has N certificates`, where N is glab's CA plus your system's CAs (164 on macOS), then `PROBE direct connection status 200` and `exit=0`.


**64. Leave the scratch directory**

body.title: feat(df): trust the proxy despite a local Bundler ssl_ca_cert
body.description:
## Description

Bundler ranks a project's local config above the environment. So an `ssl_ca_cert` set with `bundle config set --local`, the usual way to point Bundler at a company CA, outranks the CA bundle glab gives Bundler. Bundler then rejects glab's inspection proxy and fails with `Could not verify the SSL certificate`. It fails closed: nothing gets past the firewall, but nothing installs either.

When the local config sets `BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT`:

- glab finds that config the way Bundler does: `.bundle/config` in the directory of `BUNDLE_GEMFILE` or of the nearest `Gemfile` or `gems.rb`, or `config` in the directory `BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG` names.
- It points `BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG` at a temporary copy of that directory. The copy's CA file holds the user's CA and glab's bundle, and the directory's other entries, such as local plugins, are linked into the copy.
- After the run, it writes Bundler's own changes back to the user's config in one rename, with the user's CA line restored, and moves back anything Bundler added to the directory. A config that is a symlink stays one.

`bundle install --gemfile` naming another project still fails closed: Bundler keeps the user's CA.

Split from !4281 (closed), with the npm/Yarn fix in !4505 and the Poetry fix in !4503. Sam's review of this code is on !4281.

## Related Issues

Related to gitlab-org&24327

## How has this been tested?

<details><summary>Unit tests and before/after runs behind a corporate proxy</summary>

Unit tests in `internal/dependencyfirewall/pm`:

- `TestBundleConfigCACert`: the config-line parser, checked against Bundler 2.5.22.
- `TestBundleSetupFindsLocalConfig` and `TestBundleSetupLeavesOtherConfigsAlone`: finding the local config.
- `TestBundleSetupReplacesLocalConfigCACert`, `TestBundleSetupWritesBackBundlerConfigChanges`, `TestBundleSetupWritesBackThroughASymlinkedConfig` and `TestBundleSetupKeepsUserConfigWhenCALineCannotBeRestored`: the copy and write-back.
- `TestBundleSetupKeepsEntriesBundlerCreates`, `TestBundleSetupWarnsWhenACreatedEntryCannotBeSaved`, the `TestCopyEntry` tests and the warnings for an unreadable copy or CA: entries Bundler adds, and failures.
- `TestRunTrustsProxyDespiteLocalBundleConfig`: `Run` end to end.

`go test` over `internal/dependencyfirewall/...` and `internal/commands/df/...` and golangci-lint pass.

Before and after, run on !4281's last head (`bdff30ccc`), which has the same Bundler change, against `main` (`2b5d4bcb9`). The runs used real Bundler in Docker, behind a TLS-intercepting corporate proxy (mitmproxy). Its CA was set with `bundle config set --local ssl_ca_cert` and in `GLAB_CA_CERT`. "Corporate proxy" counts the requests that proxy logged during the run with the fix.

| Case | `main` | With the fix | Corporate proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bundler 2.5.22, `bundle install` from the project root | `Could not verify the SSL certificate`, exit 17 | `Bundle complete!` | 3 |
| The same, from a subdirectory | `Could not verify the SSL certificate`, exit 17 | `Bundle complete!` | 3 |

With the fix:

- When Bundler writes a setting during the run (`bundle config set --local path vendor/bundle`), the config keeps the user's CA line and gains `BUNDLE_PATH`, and no temporary directory is left.
- A symlinked `.bundle/config` stays a symlink, and its target gets the change.
- After `kill -9` of glab and Bundler mid-install, the user's config is byte-identical, and the temporary copy stays in `/tmp`.
- `bundle install --gemfile` naming another project fails with `Could not verify the SSL certificate`.

</details>


<details><summary>Manual testing steps (bash or zsh)</summary>

These steps compare this branch with `main` at the branch's base. glab and Bundler run on your machine, and mitmproxy runs in Docker as a TLS-intercepting corporate proxy on port 8081. Run them from the root of a checkout of this branch, with Docker running, in a new terminal tab: they set a fake token and proxy settings. Each step is one command, even when it spans several lines.

| Case | Steps | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 26 | Installs without glab | Installs without glab |
| B/C | 27–28 | Fails: `Could not verify the SSL certificate` | Installs |
| D | 29–30 | Bundler uses the project's CA | Bundler uses a temporary copy's CA file |
| E | 31–32 | That file holds 1 certificate | 3: the project's CA, then glab's bundle |
| F | 33–34 | Not run | The project's config is unchanged, and no copy is left |
| G | 35–36 | Not run | A setting Bundler changes reaches the project's config |
| H | 37–41 | Fails from a subdirectory | Installs from a subdirectory |
| I | 42–46 | Not run | A symlinked config stays a symlink |

**1. Name the scratch directory**

```shell
T=~/df-4504-test
```

**2. Name this checkout**

```shell
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

**3. Create the scratch directory**

```shell
mkdir -p $T/mitm
```

**4. Build this branch**

```shell
make -C $W build
```

**5. Keep this branch's binary**

```shell
cp $W/bin/glab $T/glab-branch
```

**6. Check out `main` at this branch's base**

```shell
git -C $W worktree add --detach $T/main "$(git -C $W merge-base HEAD origin/main)"
```

**7. Build `main`**

```shell
make -C $T/main build
```

**8. Keep `main`'s binary**

```shell
cp $T/main/bin/glab $T/glab-main
```

**9. Start the corporate proxy**

```shell
docker run -d --name df-4504-corp -p 127.0.0.1:8081:8080 \
  -v $T/mitm:/home/mitmproxy/.mitmproxy mitmproxy/mitmproxy mitmdump
```

Prints the container ID.

**10. Wait for the proxy to create its CA**

```shell
sleep 3
```

**11. Check that the CA exists**

```shell
ls $T/mitm/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem
```

Prints the path. If it doesn't, wait a second and run it again.


**12. Clear CA, proxy and Bundler settings from your shell**

```shell
unset SSL_CERT_FILE BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG BUNDLE_GEMFILE BUNDLE_PATH BUNDLE_USER_HOME \
  GEM_HOME GEM_PATH GLAB_CA_CERT HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY http_proxy https_proxy ALL_PROXY NO_PROXY no_proxy CI GITLAB_CI
```

**13. Check that a recent Bundler comes first on `PATH`**

```shell
bundle -v
```

Prints Bundler 2.5 or later; these steps were run with 2.7.1. If yours is older, put a newer Ruby first on `PATH`. With mise, run `export MISE_RUBY_VERSION=3.3.9` and wait for the next prompt.

**14. Name the corporate CA**

```shell
CA=$T/mitm/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem
```

**15. Point at the corporate proxy and trust its CA**

glab reads `HTTPS_PROXY`, and Bundler reads `HTTP_PROXY`. Bundler downloads `.gem` files through RubyGems, which ignores Bundler's `ssl_ca_cert` and uses `SSL_CERT_FILE`.

```shell
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8081 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8081 SSL_CERT_FILE=$CA
```

**16. Let glab allow every package without calling GitLab**

```shell
export GLAB_DF_FAKE_DEFAULT=allow GITLAB_REPO=gitlab.com/example/df-proxy-test GITLAB_TOKEN=fake
```

**17. Keep your own glab and Bundler settings out of the test**

```shell
export GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=$T/glab-config BUNDLE_USER_HOME=$T/bundle-home
```

**18. Turn off glab's telemetry and update check**

```shell
export GLAB_SEND_TELEMETRY=false GLAB_CHECK_UPDATE=false
```

**19. Define `try`**

`try` deletes the project's installed gems and lockfile, so every install downloads again, then runs the command and prints its exit code.

```shell
try() { rm -rf $T/proj/vendor $T/proj/Gemfile.lock; "$@"; echo "exit=$?"; }
```


**20. Create the project directory**

```shell
mkdir $T/proj
```

**21. Go into it**

```shell
cd $T/proj
```

**22. Write the `Gemfile`**

```shell
cat > Gemfile <<'EOF'
source "https://rubygems.org"
gem "colorize"
EOF
```

**23. Install gems inside the project**

```shell
bundle config set --local path vendor/bundle
```

**24. Point Bundler at the corporate CA in the project's config**

```shell
bundle config set --local ssl_ca_cert $CA
```

**25. Show the project's config**

```shell
cat .bundle/config
```

Prints `---`, `BUNDLE_PATH: "vendor/bundle"` and `BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT:` with the path of `$CA`.


**26. A: install without glab**

```shell
try bundle install
```

Prints `Bundle complete! 1 Gemfile dependency, 2 gems now installed.` and `exit=0`.

**27. B: install through `main`**

```shell
try $T/glab-main df bundle install
```

Prints `Could not verify the SSL certificate for https://rubygems.org/quick/Marshal.4.8/colorize-0.5.0.gemspec.rz.` and `exit=17`. Bundler uses the project's CA, which doesn't include glab's.

**28. C: install through this branch**

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df bundle install
```

Prints `Bundle complete! 1 Gemfile dependency, 2 gems now installed.` and `exit=0`.

**29. D: which `ssl_ca_cert` Bundler uses under `main`**

```shell
$T/glab-main df bundle config get ssl_ca_cert
```

Prints `Set for your local app (…/proj/.bundle/config):` with the path of `$CA`, above `Set via BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT:` with glab's `glab-df-ca-*.pem`. The top line wins: the project's config outranks the variable glab sets.

**30. D: which `ssl_ca_cert` Bundler uses under this branch**

```shell
$T/glab-branch df bundle config get ssl_ca_cert
```

Prints `Set for your local app (…/glab-df-bundle-*/bundle/config): "…/glab-df-bundle-*/ca.pem"` above the same `BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT` line. Bundler reads glab's temporary copy of the config.

**31. E: what that CA file holds under `main`**

```shell
$T/glab-main df bundle exec ruby -e 'f = Bundler.settings[:ssl_ca_cert]; puts f, File.read(f).scan("BEGIN CERTIFICATE").size'
```

Prints the path of `$CA` and `1`.

**32. E: what that CA file holds under this branch**

```shell
$T/glab-branch df bundle exec ruby -e 'f = Bundler.settings[:ssl_ca_cert]; puts f, File.read(f).scan("BEGIN CERTIFICATE").size'
```

Prints a `…/glab-df-bundle-*/ca.pem` path and `3`: the project's CA, then glab's bundle, which holds the CA from `SSL_CERT_FILE` and glab's CA. glab deletes the copy when the command ends.

**33. F: the project's config is unchanged**

```shell
cat .bundle/config
```

Prints the same lines as step 25.

**34. F: no temporary copy is left**

```shell
ls "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" | grep -c glab-df-bundle
```

Prints `0`.

**35. G: have Bundler change a setting through this branch**

```shell
$T/glab-branch df bundle config set --local without development
```

Prints nothing. Bundler writes the setting to glab's copy, and glab saves it back.

**36. G: show the project's config**

```shell
cat .bundle/config
```

Prints the lines from step 25 plus `BUNDLE_WITHOUT: "development"`. `BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT` still names `$CA`, not the copy.

**37. H: create a subdirectory**

```shell
mkdir lib
```

**38. H: go into it**

```shell
cd lib
```

**39. H: install through `main` from the subdirectory**

```shell
try $T/glab-main df bundle install
```

Prints `Could not verify the SSL certificate …` and `exit=17`.

**40. H: install through this branch from the subdirectory**

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df bundle install
```

Prints `Bundle complete! …` and `exit=0`. glab finds the project's config from the nearest `Gemfile` above, as Bundler does.

**41. H: go back to the project**

```shell
cd ..
```

**42. I: move the config elsewhere**

```shell
mv .bundle/config $T/shared-config
```

**43. I: link it back as a symlink**

```shell
ln -s $T/shared-config .bundle/config
```

**44. I: have Bundler change a setting through this branch**

```shell
$T/glab-branch df bundle config set --local jobs 4
```

Prints nothing.

**45. I: check that the config is still a symlink**

```shell
ls -l .bundle/config
```

Prints `.bundle/config -> …/shared-config`.

**46. I: show the symlink's target**

```shell
cat $T/shared-config
```

Prints the lines from step 36 plus `BUNDLE_JOBS: "4"`.


**47. Leave the scratch directory**

```shell
cd ~
```

**48. Stop the corporate proxy**

```shell
docker rm -f df-4504-corp
```

**49. Remove the `main` checkout**

```shell
git -C $W worktree remove --force $T/main
```

**50. Delete the scratch directory**

```shell
rm -rf $T
```


</details>

body.title: fix(df): trust the proxy through PIP_CERT for poetry
body.description:
## Description

glab sets `PIP_PROXY` for Poetry, so that pip run by Poetry, as with `poetry run pip install`, goes through glab's inspection proxy. But glab gave pip its CA bundle only through `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, and pip ignores `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` whenever a proxy is set with `--proxy` or `PIP_PROXY` (pip 25.0.1 and 26.3 both do). So pip never trusted the proxy, and `poetry run pip install` under `glab dependency-firewall poetry` failed for every user, whether or not they had set a CA. It failed closed: nothing got past the firewall, but nothing installed either.

The production change is Poetry's two variable lists in `poetry.go`, which now match what pip and pipenv already have in `pip.go`. The rest of the diff is the `poetryManager` doc comment and tests.

| In `poetry.go` | What it controls | `main` | This MR | Effect on the command glab runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CATrustEnviron` | Variables glab sets to its bundle for the command | `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` | `PIP_CERT`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` | pip gets `PIP_CERT`, which it reads even with `PIP_PROXY` set, so it trusts glab's proxy. glab's value replaces any `PIP_CERT` the user set. |
| `ExistingBundleVars` | Variables whose files glab merges into its bundle | `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` | `PIP_CERT`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` | The certificates in the file a user's `PIP_CERT` names go into the bundle, so the user's CA stays trusted. |

The merge itself is existing code: `writeCABundle` in `pm.go` reads each listed variable from glab's environment, and writes the certificates from those files, then glab's CA, to the bundle. A plain `poetry add` doesn't read `PIP_CERT`, so it isn't affected.

With no user CA set, the bundle holds only glab's CA. A tool that uses `PIP_CERT` to connect directly, without the proxy, therefore loses the public roots. A follow-up MR adds the system roots to the bundle.

Split from !4281 (closed), with the npm/Yarn fix in !4505 and the Bundler fix in !4504. This MR and !4505 both change `managers_test.go`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Related Issues

Related to gitlab-org&24327

## How has this been tested?

<details><summary>Unit tests and before/after runs behind a corporate proxy</summary>

Unit tests in `internal/dependencyfirewall/pm`: `TestManagerEnvironAndCATrust` and `TestManagerExistingBundleVars` cover Poetry's new `PIP_CERT`. `TestRunMergesUserCAIntoOverriddenVar` checks through `Run` that the child's `PIP_CERT` names a bundle holding the user's CA and the proxy CA. `go test` over `internal/dependencyfirewall/...` and `internal/commands/df/...` and golangci-lint pass.

Before and after, run on this branch (`078eaed74`) against `main` (`fddc76b15`), on macOS with Poetry 2.5.1 and pip 26.3. glab and Poetry ran on the host, behind a TLS-intercepting corporate proxy (mitmproxy in Docker). "Corporate proxy" counts the requests that proxy logged during the run with the fix.

| Case | `main` | With the fix | Corporate proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `poetry run pip install six`, the user's CA in `PIP_CERT` | `“glab Dependency Firewall CA” certificate is not trusted`, exit 1 | `Successfully installed six-1.17.0` | 3 |
| The same, the user's CA in `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` | Same failure | `Successfully installed six-1.17.0` | 3 |
| The same, no CA in the environment (glab trusts the corporate proxy through `GLAB_CA_CERT`) | Same failure | `Successfully installed six-1.17.0` | 3 |
| `PIP_CERT` as pip sees it, the user's CA in `PIP_CERT` | The user's file, 1 certificate | glab's bundle, 2 certificates | n/a |
| `poetry add six`, the user's CA in `PIP_CERT` | Not run | Resolves `six` and writes the lock file | 3 |

Without glab, pip installs through the corporate proxy with the user's `PIP_CERT`, so the setup itself works.

On !4281's last head (`bdff30ccc`), the same change also passed `poetry run pip install six` on Linux with Poetry 1.8.5 and 2.5.1 (pip 25.0.1), where `main` failed with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`. There, `poetry add six` installed on `main` too.

</details>


<details><summary>Manual testing steps (bash or zsh)</summary>

These steps compare this branch with `main` at the branch's base. glab and Poetry run on your machine, and mitmproxy runs in Docker as a TLS-intercepting corporate proxy on port 8081. Run them from the root of a checkout of this branch, with Docker running, in a new terminal tab: they set a fake token and proxy settings. Each step is one command, even when it spans several lines.

| Case | Steps | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 27–28 | Installs without glab | Installs without glab |
| B/C | 29–30 | `poetry run pip install` fails: glab's CA isn't trusted | Installs |
| D | 31–32 | pip's `PIP_CERT` is the user's file, 1 certificate | glab's bundle, 2 certificates |
| E | 33–36 | Fails with the user's CA in `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` | Installs |
| F | 37–40 | Fails with no CA in the environment | Installs |
| G | 41–43 | Not run | `poetry add` resolves through the proxy |

**1. Name a scratch directory**

```shell
T=~/df-4503-test
```

**2. Name this checkout**

```shell
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

**3. Create the scratch directory**

```shell
mkdir -p $T/mitm
```

**4. Build this branch**

```shell
make -C $W build
```

**5. Keep this branch's binary**

```shell
cp $W/bin/glab $T/glab-branch
```

**6. Check out `main` at this branch's base**

```shell
git -C $W worktree add --detach $T/main "$(git -C $W merge-base HEAD origin/main)"
```

**7. Build `main`**

```shell
make -C $T/main build
```

**8. Keep `main`'s binary**

```shell
cp $T/main/bin/glab $T/glab-main
```

**9. Create a virtual environment for Poetry**

```shell
python3 -m venv $T/poetry
```

**10. Install Poetry in it**

```shell
$T/poetry/bin/pip install -q poetry
```

**11. Start the corporate proxy**

```shell
docker run -d --name df-4503-corp -p 127.0.0.1:8081:8080 \
  -v $T/mitm:/home/mitmproxy/.mitmproxy mitmproxy/mitmproxy mitmdump
```

**12. Wait for the proxy to create its CA**

```shell
sleep 3
```

**13. Check that the CA exists.** Prints the path; if it doesn't, wait a second and run it again.

```shell
ls $T/mitm/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem
```

**14. Create the project directory**

```shell
mkdir $T/proj
```

**15. Go into it**

```shell
cd $T/proj
```

**16. Write `pyproject.toml`**

```shell
cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "df-4503"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = []

[tool.poetry]
package-mode = false
EOF
```

**17. Keep the project's virtual environment inside the project**

```shell
$T/poetry/bin/poetry config virtualenvs.in-project true --local
```

**18. Clear CA and proxy settings from your shell**

```shell
unset PIP_CERT REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE CURL_CA_BUNDLE SSL_CERT_FILE GLAB_CA_CERT PIP_PROXY \
  HTTP_PROXY http_proxy https_proxy ALL_PROXY NO_PROXY no_proxy CI GITLAB_CI
```

**19. Put Poetry on `PATH`**

```shell
export PATH=$T/poetry/bin:$PATH
```

**20. Send glab's traffic through the corporate proxy**

```shell
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8081
```

**21. Let glab allow every package without calling GitLab**

```shell
export GLAB_DF_FAKE_DEFAULT=allow GITLAB_REPO=gitlab.com/example/df-proxy-test GITLAB_TOKEN=fake
```

**22. Keep your own glab and Poetry settings out of the test**

```shell
export GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=$T/glab-config POETRY_CACHE_DIR=$T/poetry-cache
```

**23. Turn off update checks and telemetry**

```shell
export GLAB_SEND_TELEMETRY=false GLAB_CHECK_UPDATE=false PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1
```

**24. Name the corporate CA**

```shell
CA=$T/mitm/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem
```

**25. Define `corp`.** It counts the requests the corporate proxy has logged.

```shell
corp() { docker logs df-4503-corp 2>&1 | grep -c -E '(GET|HEAD) https://'; }
```

**26. Define `try`.** It runs a command, then prints its exit code and the number of requests the corporate proxy saw during it.

```shell
try() {
  local n=$(corp)
  "$@"
  local rc=$?
  echo "exit=$rc, corporate proxy: +$(( $(corp) - n )) requests"
}
```

**27. A: point pip at the corporate CA**

```shell
export PIP_CERT=$CA
```

**28. A: install without glab.** Expect `Successfully installed six-1.17.0` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +3 requests`.

```shell
try poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**29. B: install through `main`.** Expect `No matching distribution found for six` and `exit=1, corporate proxy: +0 requests`. On macOS, pip reports `“glab Dependency Firewall CA” certificate is not trusted`; on Linux, `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`.

```shell
try $T/glab-main df poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**30. C: install through this branch.** Expect `Successfully installed six-1.17.0` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +3 requests`.

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**31. D: the `PIP_CERT` pip sees under `main`.** Expect the path of `$CA` and `1`.

```shell
$T/glab-main df poetry run sh -c 'echo "$PIP_CERT"; grep -c "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" "$PIP_CERT"'
```

**32. D: the `PIP_CERT` pip sees under this branch.** Expect a `glab-df-ca-*.pem` file in your temporary directory and `2`: the user's CA and glab's.

```shell
$T/glab-branch df poetry run sh -c 'echo "$PIP_CERT"; grep -c "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" "$PIP_CERT"'
```

**33. E: drop `PIP_CERT`**

```shell
unset PIP_CERT
```

**34. E: put the corporate CA in `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` instead**

```shell
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=$CA
```

**35. E: install through `main`.** Expect `exit=1` and `+0`. glab sets `PIP_PROXY`, and pip ignores `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` when a proxy is set that way.

```shell
try $T/glab-main df poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**36. E: install through this branch.** Expect `exit=0` and `+3`.

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**37. F: drop `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`**

```shell
unset REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
```

**38. F: trust the corporate CA in glab only.** `GLAB_CA_CERT` covers glab's own registry connections and puts no CA variable in pip's environment.

```shell
export GLAB_CA_CERT=$CA
```

**39. F: install through `main`.** Expect `exit=1` and `+0`, for the same reason as step 35.

```shell
try $T/glab-main df poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**40. F: install through this branch.** Expect `exit=0` and `+3`.

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df poetry run pip install --no-cache-dir --force-reinstall --retries 0 six
```

**41. G: drop `GLAB_CA_CERT`**

```shell
unset GLAB_CA_CERT
```

**42. G: point pip at the corporate CA again**

```shell
export PIP_CERT=$CA
```

**43. G: add a dependency through this branch.** Expect `Writing lock file` and `exit=0, corporate proxy: +3 requests`.

```shell
try $T/glab-branch df poetry add six
```

**44. Leave the scratch directory**

```shell
cd ~
```

**45. Stop the corporate proxy**

```shell
docker rm -f df-4503-corp
```

**46. Remove the `main` checkout**

```shell
git -C $W worktree remove --force $T/main
```

**47. Delete the scratch directory**

```shell
rm -rf $T
```

</details>

body.title: chore(release): collapse Go module bumps in the Slack announcement
body.description:
## What does this MR do and why?

The v1.131.0 Slack announcement listed 17 Go module bumps one per line, and the notes were cut off at the template's 10,000-character cap (it ends mid-word in the Others section).

The Slack template now replaces every `chore(deps): update module …` line with a single count under the Dependencies heading:

```
### 📦 Dependencies
* 17 Go module updates
* **chore(deps):** update Go to 1.27.4 (c789a57e) by Jay McCure :tanuki:
```

- The Go version bump and any other dependency lines stay listed.
- The count is per commit, so a module bumped twice counts twice.
- Only the Slack post changes; the GitLab release page keeps the full list.

## How to verify

- `goreleaser check` passes.
- Rendered the Slack block template locally with goreleaser v2.18.3's `filter`/`reverseFilter`/`replace`/`split` semantics against sample notes, with and without module bumps. Without module bumps the section is unchanged.

body.title: chore(govern): derive audit event IDs with SHA-256 instead of SHA-1
body.description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Changes `deterministicUUID` in `govern audit sync` from a SHA-1 UUIDv5 to a SHA-256 UUIDv8, the name-based UUID that RFC 9562 recommends in place of v5.

This prepares for the FIPS build of glab (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4207). Under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, SHA-1 panics, so `govern audit sync` would crash. Without this change, the FIPS MR has to exempt the call from enforcement.

The ID stays deterministic and keeps the same UUID format. A new subtest pins the value, so it can't change by accident.

Related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8682

## Effect on existing data

GitLab deduplicates audit events by `cloud_event_id`. Events that an older glab already posted get a different ID when synced again, so re-syncing a session after upgrading creates duplicates, once. `govern` is experimental, so the impact should be small.

## Question for reviewers

@jeanvdw does anything on the GitLab side recompute this ID or check that it's a v5 UUID? If so, this change needs a matching server change.
